newsitem.title: USA: Fixed income funds fell in Q1 -- Lipper.
newsitem.headline: Fixed income funds fell in Q1 -- Lipper.

text.p: Lipper Analytical Services said higher interests rates and market concerns over economic growth possibly overheating hurt fixed-income mutual funds in the first quarter of 1996.

Rates and fretting about growth lead to a 0.29 percent loss in the first quarter for the average domestic long-term taxable fixed income fund, versus a gain of 2.79 percent in the 1996 fourth quarter, according to Lipper.
The loss comes after gains in the prior three quarters since the first quarter of 1996.
"The declines in the securities markets during the last week of March particularly caused fixed income funds to lose ground in their net asset values," according to Lipper.
